stories.headline: Europe will join US-brokered Ukraine peace talks, despite Russia
body: European officials will attend this week's US-mediated Russia-Ukraine peace talks in the UAE, France says.
The Kremlin had said there was no role for European powers.
France's foreign minister says Europe's voice will be heard.
stories.joke: Uninvited guests with a lot to say.
stories.vc: Any ceasefire progress could cut energy prices and open Ukraine's huge rebuilding market.

stories.headline: New Zealand's election ends with no clear winner
body: New Zealand's election gave neither the right nor the left a clear win.
Smaller parties gained ground against National and Labour, the two big parties.
Weeks of tense talks are expected to form a government.
stories.joke: Kiwis voted; now the minor parties get to name their price.
stories.vc: A longer wait for a government can delay budget and investment decisions.

stories.headline: At least 34 dead as migrant boat sinks off Senegal
body: A small boat carrying migrants and refugees sank off northwestern Senegal, killing at least 34 people.
Only one person was rescued, the interior ministry said.
Thousands have died trying to reach Spain's Canary Islands from West Africa in recent years.
stories.vc: Deadly crossings reflect a lack of jobs at home, pushing young people to risk the sea route to Europe.

stories.headline: Why India still gives free grain to 80 crore people
body: PM's economic adviser Shamika Ravi says free grain for about 80 crore people is about social protection, not just poverty.
She says growing countries everywhere build safety nets.
A recent paper says extreme poverty fell to 2.3% in 12 years.
stories.joke: Poverty fell; the ration queue didn't.
stories.vc: Free grain is one of India's biggest spending items, shaping how much room is left for other investment.

stories.headline: Govt clears ₹7,503 crore of new electronics component plants
body: The government approved 12 new projects worth ₹7,503 crore under its electronics components scheme.
They will make battery materials, copper foil, films and special ceramics.
The aim is to cut imports of key inputs for phones, batteries and chips.
stories.joke: Made in India, now including the parts inside.
stories.vc: Local component makers open a new investment theme beyond phone assembly.

stories.headline: Centre rejects Karnataka's claim of 31% ethanol in petrol
body: The petroleum ministry says all 893 fuel samples tested in 27 states and UTs met quality standards.
Oil companies questioned how Karnataka took and tested its samples.
Karnataka had said some petrol had up to 31% ethanol, above the 20% target.
stories.joke: Two labs, two answers, one confused driver.
stories.vc: The dispute matters for car makers and oil companies betting on higher ethanol blends.

stories.headline: Nvidia's board investigates CEO Jensen Huang
body: Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation after reports Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation.
Huang admitted an affair with a former executive of a Singapore chip firm and apologised.
A US memo had claimed she was recruited by Chinese intelligence.
stories.vc: Any doubt over the CEO of the world's most valuable chipmaker is a risk investors will price in.

stories.headline: Unhedged: the post-midterm stock bubble popped in a day
body: The FT's Unhedged podcast says Wednesday's post-midterm rally reversed on Thursday.
AI companies gave back the previous day's gains.
The hosts ask whether it's about Democrats in Congress or a wider move away from AI.
stories.vc: If investors are rotating out of AI, it could hit everything from chip stocks to startup valuations.

stories.headline: Sequoia partners were reportedly blindsided by Botha joining SpaceX's board
body: The FT reports Sequoia's shake-up is partly an effort to undo the legacy of former leader Roelof Botha.
The split reportedly deepened when Botha joined SpaceX's board this summer.
Some insiders call the changes an erasure of Sequoia's heritage.
stories.vc: Turmoil at a top VC firm can change how it backs startups and who leads deals.

stories.headline: Ex-Secret Service agent raises a second $250M cyber fund
body: Brightmind Partners, a two-year-old cybersecurity VC firm, is raising a second $250 million fund.
Co-founder Stephen Ward spent nine years in the Secret Service.
He openly says investors should sell stakes on the way up, not wait for IPOs.
stories.joke: From catching hackers to funding the people who stop them.
stories.vc: Specialist cyber funds keep growing as AI makes attacks more common.

stories.headline: Jefferies: an AI spending slump could spark the next gold rally
body: Jefferies' Christopher Wood says gold could rally if the AI investment boom slows sharply.
That could weaken the US economy and push the Fed to cut rates.
Gold has been trading near the low end of $3,800-4,000 an ounce.
stories.joke: Gold: the asset that wins when the robots lose.
stories.vc: A gold rebound would help Indian households, who hold huge amounts of the metal.

stories.statLabel: of KMF milk suppliers are women
stories.headline: Women are most of Karnataka's milk suppliers, and gain from price hike
body: About 5.85 lakh of KMF's 10 lakh active milk suppliers are women, KMF data shows.
The recent milk price hike gives them steadier income, a Bamul leader says.
Many use it for loans, health care and children's education.
stories.vc: Dairy co-operatives are one of rural India's biggest sources of income for women.

stories.headline: Women run fewer than 1 in 10 South Asian firms, says ILO
body: Fewer than one in ten firms in South Asia are led by women, a new ILO report says.
India is near the bottom in Asia-Pacific for women in management, above only Pakistan and Bangladesh.
Globally, women hold under a third of management jobs.
stories.vc: The ILO says firms led by women report better business results, a case for investors to push change.

stories.headline: A young Somali woman is changing how tourists see Mogadishu
body: Sucdi Abdul Fattah Abdul Khader, 23, is one of a growing number of local guides in Mogadishu.
She shows visitors beaches, historic sites and the fish market.
She wants the world to see more than violence when it thinks of her city.
stories.vc: Women in tourism jobs help build a new industry in a country rebuilding after conflict.

stories.headline: Puttur hospital to grow to 220 beds for a new medical college
body: Puttur Government Hospital in Karnataka will expand from 100 to 220 beds.
It is preparing for a new government medical college due in 2027-28.
Classes could start in November 2027 with 50 students, in a temporary building.
stories.vc: New government medical colleges add both doctors and hospital beds in smaller towns.

stories.headline: Mysuru's Amrita Kripa hospital opens a new 100-bed block
body: Amrita Kripa Multi-speciality Hospital in Mysuru opened a new 100-bed block.
It adds an ICU, modular operating theatres and dialysis units.
Bengaluru Rural MP Dr C.N. Manjunath opened it.
stories.vc: Charity-run hospitals add critical-care beds in suburbs, easing pressure on city hospitals.

stories.headline: Delhi's GTB Hospital adds 25 emergency beds for Diwali
body: GTB Hospital in Delhi set aside 25 extra beds for Diwali emergencies.
It sees 160-200 Diwali injury patients a year, mostly burns.
A special roster covers burns, plastic surgery and eye departments.
stories.vc: Festival surges show why public hospitals need spare capacity built into their plans.

stories.headline: Norris wins wet Brazil GP; Mercedes clinch constructors' title
body: Lando Norris won a wet-dry-wet Brazilian GP, his third win of the year.
Max Verstappen finished second after starting from the back.
Mercedes sealed the constructors' title, while champion Antonelli lost the lead with a spin.
stories.joke: Rain, spins and a back-of-grid charge: Brazil never disappoints.
stories.vc: A double title lifts Mercedes' prize money and sponsor value for 2027.
